# Validation set

## What's the problem?

- How well is my ML method doing? *Model assessment*
- Which method is best for our data?
- How many features should I use? Which ones? *Model selection*
- What is the uncertainty in the learned parameters?

## Validation set approach

![](../../Figures/CV-subset0.png){fig-alt="A horizontal bar representing data points with random chunks colored as either red (training set) or yellow (test set)." width="100%"}

:::::: {.columns}

::::: {.column width="55%"}

- Divide randomly into two parts:
  - Training set
  - Validation / hold-out / testing set
- Fit the model on the training set.
- Use the fitted model to predict the response for the observations in the test set.
- Evaluate the quality (for example, MSE).

:::::

# Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (LOOCV)

## The idea

![](../../Figures/LOOCV-subset0.png){fig-alt="A horizontal bar representing data points with a yellow square (test set) at the zeroth position of the bar with the rest of the bar red (training set)" width="90%"}

![](../../Figures/LOOCV-subset1.png){fig-alt="A horizontal bar representing data points with a yellow square (test set) at the first position of the bar with the rest of the bar red (training set)" width="90%"}

![](../../Figures/LOOCV-subset2.png){fig-alt="A horizontal bar representing data points with a yellow square (test set) at the second position of the bar with the rest of the bar red (training set)" width="90%"}

![](../../Figures/LOOCV-subset3.png){fig-alt="A horizontal bar representing data points with a yellow square (test set) at the third position of the bar with the rest of the bar red (training set)" width="90%"}

![](../../Figures/LOOCV-subset4.png){fig-alt="A horizontal bar representing data points with a yellow square (test set) at the fourth position of the bar with the rest of the bar red (training set)" width="90%"}

$\vdots$

![](../../Figures/LOOCV-subset29.png){fig-alt="A horizontal bar representing data points with a yellow square (test set) at the last, rightmost position of the bar with the rest of the bar red (training set)" width="90%"}

## The idea in mathy words

:::::: {.columns}

::::: {.column width="55%"}

- Remove $(x_1,y_1)$ for testing.
- Train the model on $n-1$ points: $\{(x_2,y_2), \cdots, (x_n,y_n)\}$.
- Calculate $\mathrm{MSE}_1 = (y_1-\hat y_1)^2$.
- Remove $(x_2,y_2)$ for testing.
- Train the model on $n-1$ points: $\{(x_1,y_1),(x_3,y_3), \cdots, (x_n,y_n)\}$.
- Calculate $\mathrm{MSE}_2 = (y_2-\hat y_2)^2$.
- Rinse and repeat.

:::::

::::: {.column width="40%"}

Return the score:
$$
CV_{(n)} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \mathrm{MSE}_i
$$

:::::

::::::
